name: Adjacent Degree-Three Endpoint Failure Is Equivalent to Repairing a Degree-Two Rooted Factor
statement: The following are equivalent: (1) an ample family $H$ has adjacent degree-three corners $a,c$, peels to $a$, but $H\setminus\{c\}$ does not peel to $a$; (2) a rooted factor $(T,t)$ has a degree-two corner root and admits an adjacent ample one-concept addition with acquired support three that makes peeling to $t$ possible. Both profiles occur in the certified 622-to-621 example. Hence prescribed-endpoint invariance under deleting an adjacent nonroot corner already fails in degree three.
proof: For (1), delete both adjacent corners. Either single re-addition has the same two-coordinate acquired support; square-pair invariance makes the common base ordinarily peelable, and rank-two extension invariance makes the one-corner deletion ordinarily peelable. The support-three descent theorem then produces the rooted factor in (2), with a degree-two corner root. Conversely, the added concept in (2) is a degree-three corner whose cube contains the neighboring root. The root's two old incident directions together with their new edge are precisely that cube's directions, so the root is also a degree-three corner and deleting the new corner restores endpoint failure. The existing 621-concept factor and its 622-concept repair establish existence.
